basic_info: 62 years old, male, presenting with knee joint pain following physical activity.
present_illness: The patient reports experiencing significant knee pain after moving boxes around the house over the weekend. The pain has been severe enough to disrupt sleep on Saturday night. The pain started over the weekend when moving boxes up and down the basement stairs. It got worse as the day went on, and by the end of the day, both knees were very painful. It has been sore ever since and kept the patient up on Saturday night. The patient notes that there is no swelling or redness, but the knees feel tender to the touch. The pain is more of a dull, aching sensation, especially when putting weight on them. The patient tried taking some Tylenol and icing them, but nothing really helped. The pain gets worse when putting weight on them or trying to move around a lot, like when moving boxes. It doesn't really get better with rest, and there is no clicking or locking in the knees. They just feel sore and tender all the time. The pain is mainly in the knees, both of them, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. There is some stiffness, especially in the morning, and it's hard to fully bend or straighten them without some discomfort. It feels like they're just sore and tight all the time. The pain is mainly around the front and sides of both knees. It's made it harder to walk comfortably and do things like go up and down stairs, which I haven't had much trouble with before. I've been trying to keep moving, but it's definitely slowed me down a bit.
past_history: The patient has a history of knee problems and arthritis, which he has been managing for a while. He has a history of kidney transplant, which may influence treatment options. The patient has not had any recent blood tests or inflammatory markers testing specifically for arthritis or other systemic conditions. The last time he was checked, everything seemed okay with his kidney function and thyroid levels, but he is not sure if that included inflammatory markers.
